newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: March against Venezuela's Caldera ends in violence.
newsitem.headline: March against Venezuela's Caldera ends in violence.

text.p: A march by thousands of Venezuelan workers and students against President Rafael Caldera's government ended in violence on Wednesday with small groups of protesters fighting pitched battles with police.
Police used tear gas and plastic bullets to disperse the protesters who tried to break shop fronts at the end of the march by about 5,000 people in central Caracas.
"This is an insignificant attempt at public disorder perpetrated by small groups of infiltrators," police commissioner Francisco Belisario told reporters.
At least one person, a photographer, was hurt during the brief clashes when a small explosive device blew up in his face, he said.
Three other devices were deactivated and several people arrested, Belisario added.
The march, led by striking university professors, had been largely peaceful. Protesters shouted slogans against Caldera and his ministers and carried banners criticising his economic policies.

Caldera's government has faced an increasing number of protests and strikes this year as the effects of a tough economic programme began to take their toll on Venezuelans' pockets. Annual inflation is running at more than 80 percent.
Students and police also clashed sporadically on Wednesday in Venezuela's fourth largest city Valencia, about 125 miles (200 km) west of Caracas, local radio said.
Students protesting against university funding and government policies set fire to a car and threw rocks at police.
